name: The State Of Wakanda 1
html:
Welcome reader!
Let's now move to the next problem, that is "The State Of Wakanda" of chapter "2D-Arrays"

Important Links: Question link, Question video, Solution video

How is it going with the 2D-arrays? Don't worry if you face any issues as this is just the beginning of the topic, we will take you to the depth of the 2 dimensional arrays. The only way to solve a problem or understand a concept is to do a lot of brainstorming.

Also, I have important advice for you that don't get scared or judge the difficulty level merely with the name of the problem. I know, Wakanda may sound scary; even it did to me, initially. But it's just a fictional state. Trust me, the problem is way too easy.

Don't forget to go through the problem on our website.

Let's jump to the problem.

Problem Discussion:

The historic state of Wakanda has various monuments and souvenirs which are visited by many travelers every day. The guides follow a prescribed route of visiting the monuments which improve their understanding of the relevance of each monument.

The route of the monument is fixed and expressed in a 2-d matrix where the travelers visit the prescribed next monument.

For example

1 2 3
4 5 6
7 8 9

The prescribed route and the visitors travels this path:

1->2->3->4->5->6->7->8->9

However, a certain visitor decides to travel a different path as follows:

  1. He first travels southwards till no further south places are available.
  2. He then moves only 1 place eastwards.
  3. He starts to move again towards north till any further north moves are available.

This continues till all the places are covered.

For example, the monuments are named as follows:

1 2 3
4 5 6
7 8 9

Path followed by these travelers: 1->4->7->8->5->2->3->6->9, which maps as follow:

So, if you look at the above pattern, the big scary problem condenses to a short wave traversal of a 2D-array.

First, you will be given a number n, representing the number of rows. Then, a number m, representing the number of columns. After that you will be given n*m numbers, representing elements of 2d arrays.

Our aim is to traverse this input 2D array, in a wave pattern.

Watch the question video for better understanding of what needs to be done.

Watch video Approach:
  1. First of all, take an input for n, which will be the number of rows, then m which will be the number of columns. Then you need to declare a 2D array of dimensions n*m. Now, you need to run a nested for loop for taking input for n*m elements of the 2D array.
  2. Let's assume, that user entered below values as input:
    3 4 11 12 13 14 21 22 23 24 31 32 33 34
    Which gives us a 2D array arr, shown as below:
  3. Looking at the figure, we can observe that during wave traversal, the value of the column is always increasing by one (0 1 2 3).
    Which, bring us to say that our first loop will concern columns (that is arr[0].length)

One more thing here to notice is that, value of the row is increasing in the first column and decreasing in the second and so on as we follow our wave pattern.

We can conclude that, whenever the value of a column is 0 or 2 (even), the value of row increases. And when the value of the column is 1 or 3 (odd), the value of the row decreases.

Therefore, inside for loop we first check if j is odd or even.

If j is even, then you need to run a nested for loop, initializing it with i = 0 till arr.length with an increment of one in each iteration, printing the elements of the jth column in increasing order of rows.

Else (j is odd), you need to run a nested for loop initializing it with i = (arr.length -1) till 0 with an increment of one in each iteration and printing the elements of the jth column in decreasing order of rows.

I hope that you understood this part. For a better understanding watch these parts of the solution video.

Watch video import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class state of wakanda{ public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); int m = scn.nextInt(); int[][] arr = new int[n][m]; for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < arr[0].length; j++) { arr[i][j] = scn.nextInt(); } } for (int j = 0; j < arr[0].length; j++) { if (j % 2 == 0) { for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) System.out.println(arr[i][j]); } else { for (int i = arr.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) System.out.println(arr[i][j]); } } } }
java; true"; Analysis Time Complexity:

O(n^2)

As there is nested for loop and the outer for loop runs n times. There are two inner for loops. Either one will run in each iteration.

Making the time complexity: O(n)*(O(n/2)+O(n/2))= O(n^2).

SPACE COMPLEXITY:

O(1)

Since, we are not using any auxiliary space and hence the space complexity is O(1).

So reader, we hope you understood the solution of this problem successfully. Don't worry if you are not able to understand this problem or you were not able to solve this problem by yourself initially.

Just spend more time reading and thinking about it.

However, if you still face any difficulties in the solution for the problem, you may visit the complete solution video.
